title.raw: 卷49 李靈 崔鑒 Volume 49: Li Ling, Cui Jian

sentences.zh: 李靈 崔鑒

translations.literal: Li Ling, Cui Jian
translations.idiomatic: Li Ling and Cui Jian

sentences.zh: 李靈，字虎符，趙郡人，高平公順從父兄也。

translations.literal: Li Ling, styled Hufu, was a man of Zhao Commandery; he was the elder paternal cousin of Duke Gaoping Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ling, whose courtesy name was Hufu, came from Zhao Commandery; he was the elder paternal cousin of Duke Gaoping Shun.

sentences.zh: 父勰，字小同，恬靜好學，有聲趙魏。

translations.literal: His father Xie, styled Xiaotong, was quiet and fond of learning; he had a reputation in Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie, whose courtesy name was Xiaotong, was calm and studious and enjoyed renown across Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖平中原，聞勰已亡，哀惜之，贈宣威將軍、蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor pacified the Central Plains, he heard that Xie had already died and mourned him; he posthumously granted him General Who Proclaims Might and Administrator of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu pacified the Central Plains and learned that Xie was already dead, he expressed sorrow and posthumously made him General Who Proclaims Might and administrator of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，世祖徵天下才儁，靈至，拜中書博士，轉侍郎。

translations.literal: During Shengui, the Shizu Emperor summoned talented men from throughout the realm; Ling came forward and was appointed doctrinal master in the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengui era Emperor Shizu summoned outstanding men from across the empire; Ling answered the call and was made a doctrinal master in the Masters of Writing, then promoted to attendant.

sentences.zh: 從駕臨江，除淮陽太守。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial carriage on the campaign to the Yangzi and was appointed Administrator of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the Yangzi campaign and was appointed administrator of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 靈以學優溫謹，選授高宗經。

translations.literal: Because Ling's learning was outstanding and his manner warm and careful, he was selected to instruct Emperor Gaozong in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ling's scholarship was excellent and his manner warm and careful, he was chosen to teach the classics to the future Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 後加建威將軍、中散、內博士，賜爵高邑子。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally given the titles General Who Establishes Might, Palace Writer, and Internal Doctrinal Master, and was granted the rank of Viscount of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was also made General Who Establishes Might, palace writer, and internal doctrinal master, and granted the viscountcy of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐受，除平南將軍、洛州刺史而卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Ling was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Regional Inspector of Luozhou, then died; he was sixty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, Ling was made General Who Pacifies the South and regional inspector of Luozhou, then died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 帝追悼之，贈散騎常侍、平東將軍、定州刺史，鉅鹿公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him and posthumously granted him Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou, with the title Duke of Julu; his posthumous name was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and posthumously made him cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, general who pacifies the east, and regional inspector of Dingzhou, with the title duke of Julu and the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 子恢，襲子爵。

translations.literal: His son Hui inherited the viscount's title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui succeeded to the viscountcy.

sentences.zh: 高宗以恢師傅之子，拜員外散騎常侍、安西將軍、長安鎮副將，進爵為侯，假鉅鹿公。

translations.literal: Because Hui was the son of the crown prince's tutor, Emperor Gaozong appointed him Extraordinary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the West, and deputy general of the garrison of Chang'an; his rank was advanced to marquis, and he was given the acting title Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hui was the tutor's son, Emperor Gaozong made him extraordinary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, general who pacifies the west, and deputy general of the Chang'an garrison, raised him to marquis, and granted him the acting title duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 皇興元年，鎮軍大將軍、東平王道符謀反，殺恢及雍州刺史魚玄明、雍州別駕李允等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangxing, the General Who Guards the Army, Prince of Dongping Dao Fu, plotted rebellion and killed Hui, together with Regional Inspector of Yongzhou Yu Xuanming, Vice-Prefect of Yongzhou Li Yun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangxing, Prince of Dongping Dao Fu, general who guards the army, rebelled and killed Hui along with Yu Xuanming, regional inspector of Yongzhou, Li Yun, vice-prefect of Yongzhou, and others.

sentences.zh: 恢時年四十八。

translations.literal: Hui was then forty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was forty-eight at the time.

sentences.zh: 顯祖愍之，追贈恢散騎常侍、鎮西將軍、定州刺史、鉅鹿公，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu commiserated with him and posthumously granted Hui the titles Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the West, Regional Inspector of Dingzhou, and Duke of Julu; his posthumous name was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu took pity on him and posthumously made Hui cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, general who pacifies the west, regional inspector of Dingzhou, and duke of Julu, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 恢長子悅祖，襲爵高邑侯，例降為伯。

translations.literal: Hui's eldest son Yuezu inherited the title Marquis of Gaoyi; by precedent the rank was reduced to baron.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's eldest son Yuezu succeeded to the marquisate of Gaoyi, which was reduced by precedent to a baronage.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子景威，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingwei inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingwei succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定末，西汝陰太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Administrator of Xi Runan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he served as administrator of Xi Runan.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his noble rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 悅祖弟顯甫，本州別駕，遷步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Yuezu's younger brother Xianfu was Vice-Prefect of his native province and was transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezu's younger brother Xianfu served as vice-prefect of his home province and was promoted to commandant of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 從駕南討，以功賜爵平棘子，行并州事。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial carriage on the southern campaign; for his merit he was granted the rank Viscount of Pingji and acted as administrator of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign and, for his service, was granted the viscountcy of Pingji and put in charge of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋除河北太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed administrator of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈顯武將軍、安州刺史，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he received the titles General of Manifest Martiality and Regional Inspector of Anzhou; his posthumous name was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made general of manifest martiality and regional inspector of Anzhou, with the posthumous name Wei.

sentences.zh: 子元忠，武定中，驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、晉陽縣開國伯。

translations.literal: His son Yuanzhong, during Wuding, held the titles General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Baron Who Founded the State of Jinyang County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanzhong, during Wuding, was general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the three dukes, and founding baron of Jinyang County.

sentences.zh: 子搔，武定末，河內太守。

translations.literal: His son Sao, at the end of Wuding, was Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sao served as administrator of Henei at the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 顯甫次弟華，字寧夏。

translations.literal: Xianfu's next younger brother Hua, styled Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Xianfu's next younger brother Hua, whose courtesy name was Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 初為羽林中郎、武騎侍郎、步兵校尉，轉直閤將軍、武衞將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a palace guard commander, Gentleman Cavalier Attendant of the Martial Guard, and Commandant of Footsoldiers; he was transferred to General of the Direct Gate and General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a palace guard commander, gentleman cavalier attendant of the martial guard, and commandant of footsoldiers, then became general of the direct gate and general of the martial guard.

sentences.zh: 華膂力過人，頗有將略，每從征伐，頻著軍功。

translations.literal: Hua's physical strength surpassed other men; he possessed considerable military talent, and whenever he followed on campaigns he repeatedly achieved merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was exceptionally strong and showed real military talent; on every campaign he won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 賜爵欒城子，定州驃騎長史、輔國將軍、中山太守。

translations.literal: He was granted the rank Viscount of Luancheng, and served as chief clerk to the general of agile cavalry of Dingzhou, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the viscountcy of Luancheng and served as chief clerk to the general of agile cavalry of Dingzhou, general who assists the state, and administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈前將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he received the titles General of the Vanguard and Regional Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made general of the vanguard and regional inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 有八子。

translations.literal: He had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長子構，襲爵，至通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The eldest son Gou inherited the title and rose to Unembellished Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Gou succeeded to the title and rose to unembellished cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈殷州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he received the title Regional Inspector of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made regional inspector of Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 次敬義，司徒長流參軍、兼光祿少卿、平北將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next, Jingyi, was Senior Adjutant of the Minister of Works, concurrently Vice Director of the Bureau of Glorious Affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, and Grand Master for Glorious Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Jingyi, who served as senior adjutant on the minister of works' staff, concurrently vice director of the bureau of glorious affairs, general who pacifies the north, and grand master for glorious affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本將軍、殷州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he received his former title of general and the post of Regional Inspector of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted his former rank of general and the post of regional inspector of Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 次叔向，為徐州鎧曹參軍，帶郭浦戍主。

translations.literal: The next, Shuxiang, was a staff officer in the armor bureau of Xuzhou and concurrently commandant of the Guopu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Shuxiang, who served as a staff officer in the armor bureau of Xuzhou and concurrently as commandant of the Guopu garrison.

sentences.zh: 值刺史元法僧叛，逼入蕭衍。

translations.literal: When the regional inspector Yuan Faseng rebelled, he was forced to enter the territory of Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the regional inspector Yuan Faseng rebelled, Shuxiang was compelled to go over to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 次幼緒，早亡。

translations.literal: The next, Youxu, died young.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Youxu, who died young.

sentences.zh: 次季脩，博陵、常山二郡太守。

translations.literal: The next, Jixiu, was Administrator of the two commanderies Boling and Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Jixiu, who served as administrator of Boling and Changshan.

sentences.zh: 次世幹，次稚明，兄弟並不修名行，險暴無禮，為時所賤。

translations.literal: The next were Shigan and then Zhiming; the brothers alike did not cultivate reputation and conduct—they were treacherous, violent, and without propriety, and were despised by their age.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Shigan and then Zhiming; the brothers alike neglected reputation and proper conduct, were treacherous, violent, and rude, and were despised by their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 華弟憑，字青龍。

translations.literal: Hua's younger brother Ping, styled Qinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Hua's younger brother Ping, whose courtesy name was Qinglong.

sentences.zh: 祕書主文中散，累遷冀州征東長史、太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He was a palace writer in the Secretariat and was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk on the eastern campaign staff of Jizhou and Attendant in the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a palace writer in the secretariat and rose through the posts of chief clerk on the eastern campaign staff of Jizhou and attendant in the household of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 阿附趙脩，超遷司空長史、給事黃門侍郎、武衞將軍、定州大中正。

translations.literal: He attached himself to Zhao Xiu and was promoted out of turn to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, Supervising Secretary and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, General of the Martial Guard, and Chief Rectifier of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Currying favor with Zhao Xiu, he was promoted out of turn to chief clerk of the minister of works, supervising secretary and gentleman at the yellow gate, general of the martial guard, and chief rectifier of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐脩黨免官。

translations.literal: Because of his connection with Xiu's faction he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office for belonging to Xiu's faction.

sentences.zh: 後除趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed administrator of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子道嘉，字同吉。

translations.literal: His son Daojia, styled Tongji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daojia, whose courtesy name was Tongji.

sentences.zh: 豫州外兵參軍、汝陽太守。

translations.literal: He was an external military staff officer of Yuzhou and Administrator of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an external military staff officer of Yuzhou and as administrator of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 同吉弟文衡，開府行參軍。

translations.literal: Tongji's younger brother Wenheng was a traveling staff officer in an open office.
translations.idiomatic: Tongji's younger brother Wenheng served as a traveling staff officer in an open office.

sentences.zh: 恢弟綜，行河間郡，早卒。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Zong acted as administrator of Hejian Commandery and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Zong served as acting administrator of Hejian Commandery and died young.

sentences.zh: 綜子遵，[1]字良軌，有業尚。

translations.literal: Zong's son Zun,[1] styled Lianggui, had established pursuits and ideals.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's son Zun,[1] whose courtesy name was Lianggui, had serious scholarly commitments.

sentences.zh: 初拜奉朝請、尚書度支郎。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Court Gentleman for the Dynasty and a clerk in the Revenue Section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a court gentleman for the dynasty and a clerk in the revenue section of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，為營構將。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he became Construction Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he became construction commander.

sentences.zh: 高祖南伐，為行臺郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu marched south, he served as a clerk on the mobile headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Gaozu's southern campaign he served as a clerk on the mobile headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，拜太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers in the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he was made commandant of footsoldiers in the household of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，轉步兵校尉，兼散騎侍郎副盧昶東北道使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers and concurrently served as Cavalier Attendant and deputy to Lu Chang on the northeastern-route mission.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign he became commandant of footsoldiers and concurrently served as cavalier attendant and deputy to Lu Chang on the northeastern-route embassy.

sentences.zh: 拜司空諮議，加中壘將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Consulting Member of the Minister of Works and additionally given the title General of the Central Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a consulting member on the minister of works' staff and additionally given the title general of the central rampart.

sentences.zh: 京兆王愉以征東將軍為冀州刺史，遵為愉府司馬。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, as General Who Campaigns Against the East, became Regional Inspector of Jizhou; Zun served as marshal of Yu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingzhao Yu became regional inspector of Jizhou with the title general who campaigns against the east, and Zun served as marshal of his staff.

sentences.zh: 愉反，召集州府以告之，遵不從，為愉所害。

translations.literal: When Yu rebelled, he summoned the provincial and prefectural officials to inform them; Zun would not follow him and was killed by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu rebelled he summoned the provincial and prefectural officials to join him; Zun refused and was killed by Yu.

sentences.zh: 時年四十四。

translations.literal: He was then forty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-four at the time.

sentences.zh: 事平，詔賜帛二百匹，贈征虜將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰簡，拜子渾給事中。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, an edict granted two hundred bolts of silk; posthumously he received the titles General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Regional Inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Jian, and his son Hun was appointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, an edict granted two hundred bolts of silk; he was posthumously made general who campaigns against the barbarians and regional inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Jian, and his son Hun was appointed supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 渾，字季初。

translations.literal: Hun, styled Jichu.
translations.idiomatic: Hun, whose courtesy name was Jichu.

sentences.zh: 武定末，大司農卿。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Minister of Finance.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he served as minister of finance.

sentences.zh: 渾弟繪，字敬文。

translations.literal: Hun's younger brother Hui, styled Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's younger brother Hui, whose courtesy name was Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 齊王丞相府司馬。

translations.literal: He was marshal of the Prince of Qi's chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as marshal of the Prince of Qi's chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 繪弟系，[2]字乾經。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Xi,[2] styled Ganjing.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Xi,[2] whose courtesy name was Ganjing.

sentences.zh: 少聰惠，有才學，與舅子河間邢昕少相倫輩，晚不逮之。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and bright and possessed literary learning; in youth he was a peer of his maternal nephew Xing Xin of Hejian, but in later years he did not match him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and well read; in his early years he was the equal of his maternal nephew Xing Xin of Hejian, but in later life he did not measure up to him.

sentences.zh: 初為征東法曹參軍，後除奉車都尉，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a legal bureau staff officer on the eastern campaign staff; later he was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriages and additionally given the title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a legal bureau staff officer on the eastern campaign staff, then was appointed commandant of the imperial carriages and additionally made general who pacifies the distance.

sentences.zh: 尋拜大司馬廣陵王錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed recording staff officer under the Grand Marshal, Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made a recording staff officer under the grand marshal, Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 府解，還鄉里。

translations.literal: When the office was dissolved, he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When the office was dissolved, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 徵拜冠軍將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed General Who Establishes the Champion and Palace Writer Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed general who establishes the champion and palace writer grand master.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王從子永樂為濟州刺史，聞而請與相見，待以賓交之禮。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi's nephew Yongle was Regional Inspector of Jizhou; when he heard of this he requested a meeting and treated Xi with the courtesy due a guest and companion.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu of Qi's nephew Yongle was regional inspector of Jizhou; when he heard of Xi he asked to meet him and treated him with the courtesy due an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 及永樂薨，系送葬還都。

translations.literal: When Yongle died, Xi attended the funeral and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongle died, Xi attended the funeral and then returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣使朝貢，侍中李神儁舉系為尚書南主客郎。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan sent envoys to offer tribute, Palace Attendant Li Shenjun recommended Xi for the post of Southern Host Master in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan sent envoys with tribute, Palace Attendant Li Shenjun recommended Xi for the post of southern host master in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 系前後接對凡十八人，頗為稱職。

translations.literal: Xi in all received and responded to eighteen envoys, and performed the duty quite competently.
translations.idiomatic: Xi received and entertained eighteen envoys in all and proved quite competent in the role.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王攝選，以系為司徒諮議參軍，因謂之曰：「自郎署至此，所謂不次，以卿人才，故有此舉耳。」

translations.literal: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi assumed charge of selections, he made Xi a Consulting Member of the Household of the Minister of Works, and said to him: "From the bureau offices to this post, one might call it an exceptional promotion; it is because of your talent that this appointment has been made."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi took charge of appointments, he made Xi a consulting member on the minister of works' staff and told him, "To rise from the bureau ranks to here is what people call an exceptional promotion—it is because of your talent that you have received it."

sentences.zh: 尋加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was also made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 武定五年，兼散騎常侍使蕭衍，與其二兄前後將命，時人稱之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wuding he served concurrently as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary on a mission to Xiao Yan; together with his two elder brothers he went on embassies in succession, and men of the time praised them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wuding he served concurrently as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary on a mission to Xiao Yan; he and his two elder brothers went on embassies in succession, and contemporaries praised them.

sentences.zh: 太尉高岳出討，以系為大都督司馬。

translations.literal: When Grand Commandant Gao Yue marched out on campaign, he made Xi marshal of the area commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Gao Yue marched out on campaign, he made Xi marshal of the area commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 師還，拜太子家令。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was appointed director of the household of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年八月卒，時年四十六，時人傷惜之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year he died; he was then forty-six years old, and men of the time mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the seventh year at the age of forty-six, and contemporaries mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 齊初，贈平東將軍、北徐州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Regional Inspector of North Xuzhou; his posthumous name was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qi he was posthumously made general who pacifies the east and regional inspector of North Xuzhou, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 靈弟均，趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Ling's younger brother Jun was Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's younger brother Jun served as administrator of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 均子璨，字世顯。

translations.literal: Jun's son Can, styled Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Can, whose courtesy name was Shixian.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺五寸，衣貌魁偉。

translations.literal: His height was eight feet five inches; in dress and appearance he was imposing and grand.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet five inches tall and cut an imposing figure in dress and bearing.

sentences.zh: 受學於梁祚。

translations.literal: He received instruction from Liang Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liang Zuo.

sentences.zh: 興安中，為祕書中散、本州別駕，轉趙郡、常山二郡太守。

translations.literal: During Xing'an he was a palace writer in the Secretariat and Vice-Prefect of his native province; he was transferred to Administrator of the two commanderies Zhao and Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: During Xing'an he served as a palace writer in the secretariat and vice-prefect of his home province, then became administrator of Zhao and Changshan.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，雅為高允所知。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and was well known to Gao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman of the Masters of Writing and won the esteem of Gao Yun.

sentences.zh: 天安初，劉彧徐州刺史薛安都舉彭城降，詔鎮南大將軍、博陵公尉元，鎮東將軍、城陽公孔伯恭等率眾迎之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an, Liu Yu's Regional Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu raised Pengcheng in surrender; an edict ordered the General Who Guards the South, Duke of Boling Wei Yuan, the General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong, and others to lead troops to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tian'an, Xue Andu, Liu Yu's regional inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered Pengcheng; an edict ordered Duke of Boling Wei Yuan, general who guards the south, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong, and others to lead troops to receive him.

sentences.zh: [3]顯祖復以璨參二府軍事。

translations.literal: [3] Emperor Xianzu again had Can participate in the military affairs of both commands.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Emperor Xianzu again had Can take part in the military affairs of both commands.

sentences.zh: 軍達九里山，安都率文武出迎，元不加禮接。

translations.literal: When the army reached Jiuli Mountain, Andu led civil and military officials out to welcome them, but Yuan did not extend ceremonial reception.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Jiuli Mountain, Andu came out with his civil and military officials to welcome them, but Yuan offered no proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 安都還城，使遂不至。

translations.literal: Andu returned to the city, and the envoys therefore did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Andu returned to the city, and as a result the envoys never came.

sentences.zh: 時劉彧將張永、沈攸之等率眾先屯下礚，元令璨與中書郎高閭入彭城說安都，安都即與俱載赴軍。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu's generals Zhang Yong, Shen Youzhi, and others led troops and were first encamped at Xiaqi; Yuan ordered Can and Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Gao Lu to enter Pengcheng and persuade Andu, and Andu at once rode with them to the army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yu's generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi had encamped at Xiaqi; Yuan sent Can and gentleman of the Masters of Writing Gao Lu into Pengcheng to persuade Andu, and Andu at once rode with them to the army.

sentences.zh: 元等入城，收管籥。

translations.literal: Yuan and the others entered the city and took control of the keys and seals.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and his men entered the city and took control of the keys and seals.

sentences.zh: 其夜，永攻南門不克，退還。

translations.literal: That night Yong attacked the south gate but could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yong attacked the south gate, failed to break through, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時永輜重在武原，璨勸元乘永之失據，攻永米船，大破之，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: At that time Yong's baggage train was at Wuyuan; Can urged Yuan to seize Yong's loss of a secure position, attack Yong's grain boats, and inflict a great defeat, beheading several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's baggage train was then at Wuyuan; Can urged Yuan to exploit Yong's loss of a secure position, attack his grain boats, and inflict a crushing defeat, beheading several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時大雪寒，永軍凍死者萬計，於是遂定淮北。

translations.literal: At that time heavy snow made the cold severe; in Yong's army those who froze to death numbered in the tens of thousands, and thereby the north of the Huai was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow and bitter cold followed; tens of thousands in Yong's army froze to death, and the north bank of the Huai was thereby secured.

sentences.zh: 加璨寧朔將軍，與張讜對為兗州刺史，綏安初附。

translations.literal: Can was additionally given the title General Who Pacifies the North; together with Zhang Tan he served in counterpart as Regional Inspector of Yanzhou, pacifying and settling the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Can was additionally made general who pacifies the north and, together with Zhang Tan, served as counterpart regional inspectors of Yanzhou, pacifying the newly submitted population.

sentences.zh: 以參定徐州之功，賜爵始豐侯，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: For his merit in settling Xuzhou he was granted the title Marquis of Shifeng and additionally given the title General Who Establishes Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in securing Xuzhou he was granted the marquisate of Shifeng and additionally made general who establishes martiality.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，年四十，卒，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, at age forty he died; his posthumous name was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxing year 1 he died at the age of forty; he was given the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 子元茂，太和八年襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yuanmao inherited the title in the eighth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanmao succeeded to the title in Taihe year 8.

sentences.zh: 加建武將軍。

translations.literal: He was additionally given the title General Who Establishes Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made general who establishes martiality.

sentences.zh: 以寬雅著稱。

translations.literal: He was famed for magnanimity and refinement.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for his magnanimity and refinement.

translations.literal: 〈Lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Lacuna in the text.〉

sentences.zh: 又例降。

translations.literal: Again his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was again reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 拜司徒司馬，尋除振威將軍、南征別將、彭城鎮副將，民吏安之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal of the Minister of Works; soon he was removed and made General Who Shakes Might, Separate Commander for the Southern Campaign, and Deputy General of the Pengcheng Garrison, and the people and officials were settled and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand marshal of the minister of works; soon afterward he was made general who shakes might, separate commander for the southern campaign, and deputy general of the Pengcheng garrison, and both people and officials found security under his rule.

sentences.zh: 賞帛百匹、穀二百斛。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with one hundred bolts of silk and two hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with one hundred bolts of silk and two hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年，年四十四，卒，贈顯武將軍、徐州刺史，諡曰順。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taihe, at age forty-four he died; posthumously he received the titles General of Manifest Martiality and Regional Inspector of Xuzhou; his posthumous name was Shun.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 20 he died at the age of forty-four; posthumously he was made general of manifest martiality and regional inspector of Xuzhou, with the posthumous name Shun.

sentences.zh: 子秀之，字鳳起。

translations.literal: His son Xiuzhi, styled Fengqi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiuzhi, whose courtesy name was Fengqi.

sentences.zh: 初除京兆王參軍，轉員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed staff officer to the Prince of Jingzhao; he was transferred to Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was first made a staff officer to the Prince of Jingzhao, then promoted to extraordinary attendant cavalier in ordinary.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，拜尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was appointed Director of Cases in the Ministry of Justice under the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the title and was appointed director of cases in the ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 秀之弟子雲，字鳳昇。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's younger brother's son Yun, styled Fengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's nephew Yun, whose courtesy name was Fengsheng.

sentences.zh: 司空參軍，轉外兵參軍、本州治中。

translations.literal: He was a staff officer to the Minister of Works; he was transferred to external forces staff officer and Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a staff officer to the minister of works, then as external forces staff officer and rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 子雲弟子羽，字鳳降。

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother's son Yu, styled Fengjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's nephew Yu, whose courtesy name was Fengjiang.

sentences.zh: 征南法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Legal clerk on the Southern Campaign staff.
translations.idiomatic: He served as legal clerk on the southern campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 子羽弟子岳，字鳳跱。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother's son Yue, styled Fengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's nephew Yue, whose courtesy name was Fengzhi.

sentences.zh: 員外郎、大司馬祭酒。

translations.literal: Extraordinary Gentleman and Libationer to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He served as extraordinary gentleman and libationer to the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 秀之等早孤，事母孝謹，兄弟並容貌魁偉，風度審正，而皆早卒。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi and the others were orphaned early; they served their mother filially and carefully; the brothers were all imposing in appearance and dignified in bearing, yet all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi and his cousins were orphaned early, served their mother with filial care, and were all imposing in appearance and dignified in bearing, yet each died young.

sentences.zh: 鳳昇子道宗，武定末，直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Fengsheng's son Daozong, at the end of Wuding, was General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng's son Daozong served as general of the direct gate at the end of the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 道宗弟道林，司徒中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Daozong's younger brother Daolin was a central military staff officer of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong's younger brother Daolin served as a central military staff officer under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 元茂弟宣茂，太和初，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Yuanmao's younger brother Xuanmao, at the beginning of Taihe, was appointed doctrinal master in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmao's younger brother Xuanmao was appointed a doctrinal master in the Masters of Writing at the beginning of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司空諮議，轉司馬，監營構事。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to counsellor of the Minister of Works, transferred to marshal, and supervised construction affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to counsellor of the minister of works, then made marshal and put in charge of construction projects.

sentences.zh: 出除寧朔將軍，試守正平郡，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed outside the capital as General Who Pacifies the North and acting administrator of Zhengping commandery; he declined the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who pacifies the north and acting administrator of Zhengping, but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 兼定州大中正。

translations.literal: Concurrently Chief Rectifier of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as chief rectifier of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐受鄉人財貨，為御史所劾，除名為民。

translations.literal: Because he had accepted goods from fellow villagers, he was impeached by the censor and stripped of rank and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting goods from fellow villagers he was impeached by the censor, stripped of rank, and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 從駕征新野，又從討樊鄧。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial carriage on the campaign against Xinye and also followed the campaign against Fan and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the campaign against Xinye and also took part in the campaign against Fan and Deng.

sentences.zh: 持節、兼散騎常侍、東南二道使。

translations.literal: Bearer of the staff, concurrently Regular Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary and envoy for the two southeastern routes.
translations.idiomatic: He served as bearer of the staff, concurrently regular attendant cavalier in ordinary and envoy for the two southeastern routes.

sentences.zh: 景明中，除平陽太守，以罪左遷步兵校尉。

translations.literal: During Jingming he was appointed Administrator of Pingyang; because of a crime he was demoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingming era he was made administrator of Pingyang, then demoted to commandant of footsoldiers for an offense.

sentences.zh: 正始初，除太中大夫，遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace and was transferred to Grand Master for Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengshi era he was made grand master of the palace, then promoted to grand master for splendor.

sentences.zh: 宣茂議明堂之制，以五室為長，與游肇往復，肇善之。

translations.literal: Xuanmao debated the design of the Bright Hall, holding that five chambers were superior; he exchanged arguments back and forth with You Zhao, and Zhao approved his view.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmao argued for a Bright Hall design centered on five chambers; he and You Zhao debated the point back and forth, and Zhao approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷平東將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Regional Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who pacifies the east and regional inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanchang he died at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanchang year 2 at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 遺言薄葬。

translations.literal: In his testament he requested a simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions calling for a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、齊州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously he received his former title of general and the post of Regional Inspector of Qizhou; his posthumous name was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted his former rank of general and the post of regional inspector of Qizhou, with the posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 子藉之，字脩遠。

translations.literal: His son Jiezhi, styled Xiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiezhi, whose courtesy name was Xiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 性謹正，粗涉書史。

translations.literal: His nature was careful and upright, and he had a rough acquaintance with history and literature.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful and upright by nature and had a modest grounding in history and literature.

sentences.zh: 歷員外郎、給事中、司徒諮議參軍、前將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Extraordinary Gentleman, Supervising Secretary, Counsellor Staff Officer to the Minister of Works, General of the Vanguard, and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served as extraordinary gentleman, supervising secretary, counsellor staff officer to the minister of works, general of the vanguard, and grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 著忠誥一篇，文多不載。

translations.literal: He authored one treatise, Loyal Admonition; much of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote one treatise, Loyal Admonition, but most of the text is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 永熙初卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he died at age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Yongxi era at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈中軍將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he received the titles General of the Central Army and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made general of the central army and regional inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子徹，字伯倫。

translations.literal: His son Che, styled Bolun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che, whose courtesy name was Bolun.

sentences.zh: 武定末，司空主簿。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was chief clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he served as chief clerk to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 藉之弟志，字敬遠，有氣尚。

translations.literal: Jiezhi's younger brother Zhi, styled Jingyuan, had spirit and high aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhi's younger brother Zhi, whose courtesy name was Jingyuan, was spirited and high-minded.

sentences.zh: 州主簿。

translations.literal: Provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He served as provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 子長瑜，郡功曹。

translations.literal: His son Changyu was commandery merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changyu served as commandery merit clerk.

sentences.zh: 敬遠弟幼遠，性粗暴，每為劫盜，刺史錄殺之。

translations.literal: Jingyuan's younger brother Youyuan was rough and violent by nature; he repeatedly committed robbery, and the regional inspector apprehended and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan's younger brother Youyuan was rough and violent by nature and repeatedly turned to robbery; the regional inspector had him arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 宣茂弟叔胤，舉秀才，著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Xuanmao's younger brother Shuyin passed the provincial examination as Presented Scholar and was an assistant in the Office of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmao's younger brother Shuyin passed the provincial examination as presented scholar and served as an assistant in the office of composition.

sentences.zh: 歷廣陵王諮議、南趙郡太守。

translations.literal: He held the posts of counsellor to the Prince of Guangling and Administrator of Nan Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as counsellor to the Prince of Guangling and administrator of Nan Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 在位九載，有政績。

translations.literal: Nine years in office; he had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for nine years and achieved a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 景明三年卒，年三十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingming he died at age thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingming year 3 at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 諡曰惠。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 子弼，字延軌。

translations.literal: His son Bi, styled Yanji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bi, whose courtesy name was Yanji.

sentences.zh: 位至相州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He rose to the post of recording clerk of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as recording clerk of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 弼弟翼，字景業。

translations.literal: Bi's younger brother Yi, styled Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's younger brother Yi, whose courtesy name was Jingye.

sentences.zh: 初為盪寇將軍、齋帥。

translations.literal: At first he was General Who Sweeps Bandits and fasting attendant chief.
translations.idiomatic: He began as general who sweeps bandits and fasting attendant chief.

sentences.zh: 又除員外郎，遷尚書郎，仍齋帥。

translations.literal: Again he was appointed Extraordinary Gentleman, was transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and remained fasting attendant chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made extraordinary gentleman, promoted to gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and continued as fasting attendant chief.

sentences.zh: 建義初，遇害河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he met his death at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈平北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he received the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made general who pacifies the north and regional inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 叔胤弟仲胤，自中書學生，歷公府主簿、從事中郎、諫議大夫、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Shuyin's younger brother Zhongyin, from a student in the Masters of Writing school, held the posts of chief clerk in ducal offices, attendant gentleman, Remonstrating and Advising Grandee, and Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyin's younger brother Zhongyin entered through the Masters of Writing school and served as chief clerk in ducal offices, attendant gentleman, remonstrating and advising grandee, and left assistant in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 卒，賜帛一百匹、布五十匹、綿五十斤，贈鎮遠將軍、光州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: When he died he was granted one hundred bolts of silk, fifty bolts of cloth, and fifty jin of cotton; posthumously he received the titles General Who Pacifies the Distant and Regional Inspector of Guangzhou; his posthumous name was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was granted one hundred bolts of silk, fifty bolts of cloth, and fifty jin of cotton; posthumously he was made general who pacifies the distant and regional inspector of Guangzhou, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 少子子仁，尚書主客郎。

translations.literal: The youngest son Ziren was Master of Receptions in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son, Ziren, served as master of receptions in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 崔鑒，字神具，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Jian, styled Shenju, was a man of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jian, whose courtesy name was Shenju, came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 父綽，少孤，學行修明，有名於世。

translations.literal: His father Chuo was orphaned young; his learning and conduct were cultivated and bright, and he had a name in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuo lost his parents early; his scholarship and conduct were cultivated and bright, and he enjoyed renown in the world.

sentences.zh: 與盧玄、高允、李靈等俱被徵，語在允傳。

translations.literal: Together with Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, Li Ling, and others he was all summoned to court; the account is in the biography of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court together with Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, Li Ling, and others; the account is given in Gao Yun's biography.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老固辭，後為郡功曹而卒。

translations.literal: Soon, because his mother was old, he firmly declined; later he served as commandery merit clerk and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing his aged mother, he firmly declined the appointment; he later served as commandery merit clerk and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 鑒頗有文學，自中書博士轉侍郎。

translations.literal: Jian had considerable literary learning; from doctrinal master in the Masters of Writing he was transferred to attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had considerable literary attainments; he rose from doctrinal master in the Masters of Writing to attendant.

sentences.zh: 延興中受詔使齊州，觀省風俗，行兗州事。

translations.literal: During Yanxing he received an edict to serve as envoy to Qi province, observe local customs, and administer the affairs of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanxing he was ordered on a mission to Qi province to observe local customs and administer Yanzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵桐廬縣子。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the rank Viscount of Tonglu County.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was granted the viscountcy of Tonglu county.

sentences.zh: 出為奮威將軍、東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed outside the capital as General Who Stirs Valor and Regional Inspector of East Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who stirs valor and regional inspector of East Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 鑒欲安悅新附，民有年老者，表求假以守、令，詔從之。

translations.literal: Jian wished to settle and please the newly submitted; among the people were elderly who memorialized requesting provisional appointment as administrators and magistrates, and an edict followed their request.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to settle and reassure the newly submitted population, Jian allowed elderly locals who memorialized requesting provisional appointment as commandery administrators and county magistrates; an edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 又於州內冶銅以為農具，兵民獲利。

translations.literal: Also within the province he smelted copper to make farm tools, and soldiers and people profited.
translations.idiomatic: He also had copper smelted within the province to make farm tools, to the profit of both soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、青州刺史、安平侯，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Establishes the Champion, Regional Inspector of Qingzhou, and Marquis of Anping; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made general who establishes the champion, regional inspector of Qingzhou, and marquis of Anping, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 子合，字貴和，少有時譽。

translations.literal: His son He, styled Guihe, in youth had contemporary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son He, whose courtesy name was Guihe, enjoyed a fine reputation even in youth.

sentences.zh: 襲爵桐廬子，為中書學生、主文中散、太尉諮議參軍、本州大中正。

translations.literal: He inherited the rank Viscount of Tonglu, and served as student in the Masters of Writing school, palace writer attendant, counsellor staff officer to the Grand Marshal, and Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to the viscountcy of Tonglu and served as a student in the Masters of Writing school, palace writer attendant, counsellor staff officer to the grand marshal, and chief rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 出為常山太守，卒於郡，時年二十七。

translations.literal: He was appointed outside the capital as Administrator of Changshan and died in the commandery; he was twenty-seven at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Changshan and died in office at the age of twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 長子脩義，有風望，襲爵。

translations.literal: The eldest son Xiuyi had moral prestige and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Xiuyi enjoyed moral prestige and succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 自司徒默曹參軍再遷寧遠將軍、新野太守。

translations.literal: From silent affairs staff officer of the Minister of Works he was twice promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: From silent affairs staff officer under the minister of works he was promoted twice to general who pacifies the distant and administrator of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 還，除太尉掾，出為冀州征東府長史。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed staff member to the Grand Marshal; he was appointed outside the capital as chief secretary of the Eastern Campaign staff of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made a staff member to the grand marshal, then appointed chief secretary of the eastern campaign staff of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十五。

translations.literal: He died at age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 長子放寬，襲爵。

translations.literal: The eldest son Fangkuan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Fangkuan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took the throne, his rank was reduced by precedent.

sentences.zh: 合弟秉，少有志氣。

translations.literal: He's younger brother Bing, in youth had will and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He's younger brother Bing was spirited and resolute even in youth.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為中書學生，拜奉朝請，轉徐州安東府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: During Taihe he was a student in the Masters of Writing school, was appointed Attendant at Court, and was transferred to recording clerk of the Andong staff of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe he entered the Masters of Writing school, was made attendant at court, and was transferred to recording clerk of the Andong staff of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 陽平王頤之為定州，[4]秉復為衞軍府錄事參軍，帶毋極令。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yangping Yizhi served at Dingzhou, [4] Bing again became recording clerk of the Guard Army command, concurrently magistrate of Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yangping Yizhi served at Dingzhou, [4] Bing again became recording clerk of the guard army command, concurrently serving as magistrate of Wuji.

sentences.zh: 時甄琛為長史，因公事言競之間，秉以拳擊琛，墜於牀下。

translations.literal: At that time Zhen Chen was chief secretary; during public business a verbal dispute arose between them, and Bing struck Chen with his fist and knocked him from the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Chen was then chief secretary; during a dispute over official business Bing punched him and knocked him off the bed.

sentences.zh: 琛以本縣長，笑而不論。

translations.literal: Because Chen was magistrate of this county, he laughed and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of the county Chen only laughed and let the matter pass.

sentences.zh: 其豪率若此。

translations.literal: His bold forthrightness was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his bold and unrestrained character.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰征壽春，秉從行，招致壯俠，以為部卒。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Pengcheng Xie campaigned against Shouchun, Bing followed on the expedition, recruited gallant bravos, and made them company soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Pengcheng Xie campaigned against Shouchun, Bing accompanied him, recruited bold adventurers, and enrolled them as company soldiers.

sentences.zh: 勰目之，謂左右曰：「吾當寄膽氣於此人。」

translations.literal: Xie fixed his gaze on him and said to those beside him: "I shall entrust my bold spirit to this man."
translations.idiomatic: Xie looked him over and told his attendants, "I mean to place my courage in this man's keeping."

sentences.zh: 後為司空主簿，轉掾、城門校尉、長兼司空司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was made Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, transferred to secretary, Commandant of the City Gates, and senior concurrently Grand Marshal of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief clerk of the minister of works, then as secretary, commandant of the city gates, and senior staff member concurrently serving as grand marshal of the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 遷長史，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief secretary and additionally given the title General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief secretary and additionally made general who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 出除左將軍、廣平內史，大納財貨，為清論所鄙。

translations.literal: He was appointed outside the capital as Left General and Internal Administrator of Guangping; he greatly accepted bribes and was despised by men of pure discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left general and internal administrator of Guangping, accepted bribes on a large scale, and was scorned by men of critical opinion.

sentences.zh: 入為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He entered court as Left Chief Secretary of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as left chief secretary of the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除平東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master for Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made general who pacifies the east and grand master for splendor.

sentences.zh: 尋加安西將軍，出除燕州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given the title General Who Pacifies the West and was appointed outside the capital as Regional Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also made general who pacifies the west and appointed regional inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時天下多事，遂為杜洛周攻圍。

translations.literal: At that time the realm had many troubles, and he was then besieged by Du Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was then in turmoil, and he came under siege by Du Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 秉堅守歷年，朝庭遣都督元譚與秉第二子仲哲赴救。

translations.literal: Bing defended steadfastly for years; the court sent Commander-in-Chief Yuan Tan and Bing's second son Zhongzhe to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Bing held out steadfastly for years until the court sent Commander Yuan Tan and Bing's second son Zhongzhe to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 譚敗，仲哲死之。

translations.literal: Tan was defeated, and Zhongzhe died in the effort.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was defeated and Zhongzhe was killed in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 秉遂率城民奔定州，坐免官。

translations.literal: Bing then led the people of the city in flight to Dingzhou and was dismissed from office as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Bing then led the city's people in flight to Dingzhou and was dismissed from office as punishment.

sentences.zh: 尋除撫軍將軍，行相州事，轉征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, acted as administrator of Xiangzhou affairs, and was transferred to General Who Campaigns Against the East and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made general who pacifies the army, put in charge of Xiangzhou affairs, and then promoted to general who campaigns against the east and grand master of the golden seal and purple radiance.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，冀州流民聚於河外，因立東冀州，除秉為刺史，加征東將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang, displaced persons from Ji Province gathered beyond the Yellow River, and in consequence Eastern Ji Province was established; Bing was appointed regional inspector and additionally given the title General Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xiaochang era, refugees from Ji Province gathered beyond the Yellow River, and Eastern Ji Province was established; Bing was appointed its regional inspector and additionally made general who campaigns east.

sentences.zh: 不之任。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，遷衞將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an he was transferred to General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an he was transferred to general of the guard and right grand master of splendor.

sentences.zh: 秉年老被疾，上表辭事，詔不許。

translations.literal: Bing was old and afflicted with illness; he submitted a memorial resigning office, but an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was old and ill; he submitted a memorial asking to resign, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，秉避居陽武。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Bing withdrew and took refuge at Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Bing withdrew and took refuge at Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 二年，除散騎常侍、車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, general of chariots and cavalry, and left grand master of splendor.

sentences.zh: 太昌中，除驃騎大將軍、[5]儀同三司，常侍、左光祿如故。

translations.literal: During Taichang he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, [5] Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes; his posts as Regular Attendant and Left Grand Master of Splendor remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: During Taichang he was made general of agile cavalry, [5] equal in honor to the three dukes; his posts as regular attendant and left grand master of splendor remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 頻以老病乞解。

translations.literal: Repeatedly, on grounds of age and illness, he begged to be released from office.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to be relieved on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年去職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he left office.

sentences.zh: 天平四年薨，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he died; he was seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Tianping at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、都督定瀛滄三州諸軍事、本將軍、尚書令、司徒公、定州刺史，諡曰靖穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ding, Ying, and Cang provinces, his former title as general, Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou; his posthumous name was Jingmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ding, Ying, and Cang provinces, general with his former title, director of the masters of writing, duke of the ministry of works, and regional inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous name Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 長子忻，字伯悅，有世幹。

translations.literal: The eldest son Xin, styled Boyue, had inherited family talent.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Xin, whose courtesy name was Boyue, had inherited family talent.

sentences.zh: 為荊州平南府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: He served as external military staff officer of the Pacify-the-South command of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as external military staff officer on the pacify-the-south staff of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 北道行臺常景引為行臺郎，又啟除員外郎，復為安遠將軍、尚書左中兵郎中。

translations.literal: Chang Jing of the Northern Route Mobile Headquarters recruited him as a clerk on the mobile staff; he also submitted a request appointing him Extraordinary Gentleman; he again served as General Who Pacifies the Distance and Director of the Central Military Bureau of the Left in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jing of the northern route mobile headquarters recruited him as a mobile staff clerk; he also had him appointed extraordinary gentleman, and Xin again served as general who pacifies the distance and director of the central military bureau on the left in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 以鄭儼之甥，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: As nephew of Zheng Yan, he concurrently served as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: As Zheng Yan's nephew, he concurrently served as left assistant director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害於河陰，年四十二。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin; he was forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮軍將軍、殿中尚書、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted General Who Guards the Army, Director of the Palace Masters of Writing, and Regional Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who guards the army, director of the palace masters of writing, and regional inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 忻弟仲哲。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Zhongzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother Zhongzhe.

sentences.zh: 生為祖母宋氏所養，早有知識，六歲宋亡，啼慕不止，見者悲之。

translations.literal: From birth he was reared by his grandmother née Song; early on he showed understanding. When Song died he was six; he wept and mourned incessantly, and those who saw it were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was raised by his grandmother, Lady Song; he showed understanding early. When she died he was six years old and wept incessantly; all who saw him were moved.

sentences.zh: 性恢達，常以將略自許。

translations.literal: By nature he was broad-minded and unconstrained; he often considered himself gifted in military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was open and magnanimous and often considered himself skilled in military strategy.

sentences.zh: 辟司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as mobile staff officer under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as a mobile staff officer under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 假寧朔將軍、統軍，從廣陽王淵北討，擊柔玄賊，破之，賜爵安平縣男。

translations.literal: Provisionally made General Who Pacifies the North and Commander of Armies, he followed Prince of Guangyang Yuan on the northern campaign, struck the Rouxuan bandits, defeated them, and was granted the title Baron of Anping County.
translations.idiomatic: Provisionally made general who pacifies the north and army commander, he followed Prince of Guangyang Yuan on the northern campaign, defeated the Rouxuan bandits, and was granted the barony of Anping County.

sentences.zh: 及父秉於燕州被圍，泣訴朝庭，遂除別將，與都督元譚赴援。

translations.literal: When his father Bing was besieged at Yanzhou, he wept and pleaded to the court; he was then appointed separate commander and went with Commander Yuan Tan to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Bing was besieged at Yanzhou, he wept and appealed to the court; he was then made a separate commander and went with Commander Yuan Tan to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 到下口，遇賊，仲哲戰歿，時年三十五。

translations.literal: Reaching Xiakou, they encountered bandits; Zhongzhe died in battle; he was thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiakou they met the enemy; Zhongzhe was killed in battle at the age of thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 長子長瑜，武定中，儀同開府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: The eldest son Zhangyu, during Wuding, was middle military staff officer of an opening office of equal honor.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Zhangyu, during Wuding, served as middle military staff officer on an equal-honor opening office staff.

sentences.zh: 長瑜弟叔瓚，司徒田曹參軍。

translations.literal: Zhangyu's younger brother Shuguan was field affairs staff officer under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangyu's younger brother Shuguan served as field affairs staff officer under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 仲哲弟叔彥，撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Zhongzhe's younger brother Shuyan was General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhe's younger brother Shuyan was general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 叔彥弟季通，武定中，兼司農少卿。

translations.literal: Shuyan's younger brother Jitong, during Wuding, concurrently served as Vice Director of the Minister of Finance.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan's younger brother Jitong, during Wuding, concurrently served as vice director of the minister of finance.

sentences.zh: 季通小弟季良，風望閑雅。

translations.literal: Jitong's youngest brother Jiliang had a serene and elegant reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Jitong's youngest brother Jiliang had a serene and elegant reputation.

sentences.zh: 自太學博士從都督李神軌征討有功，賜爵蒲陰縣男。

translations.literal: From his post as erudite of the Imperial Academy he followed Commander Li Shengui on a punitive campaign with merit and was granted the title Baron of Puyin County.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as an erudite of the imperial academy he followed Commander Li Shengui on campaign with merit and was granted the barony of Puyin County.

sentences.zh: 尋除著作佐郎、通直散騎侍郎，轉征虜將軍、員外散騎常侍、太尉長史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Assistant in the Office of Composition and Unembellished Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he was transferred to General Who Campaigns against the Barbarians, Extraordinary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Chief Secretary to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made assistant in the office of composition and unembellished attendant of the scattered cavalry, then transferred to general who campaigns against the barbarians, extraordinary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and chief secretary to the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 及秉還鄉，季良亦去職歸養。

translations.literal: When Bing returned to his home district, Jiliang also left office to return home and care for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing returned home, Jiliang also left office to go home and care for him.

sentences.zh: 後除中軍將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Central Army and Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made general of the central army and grand master of splendor.

sentences.zh: 先秉卒於家，時年三十六。

translations.literal: He predeceased Bing, who later died at home; he was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Bing, who later died at home; he was thirty-six at the time.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍、尚書右僕射、定州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Regional Inspector of Dingzhou; his posthumous name was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general of chariots and cavalry, right vice director of the masters of writing, and regional inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 秉弟習，字貴禮，有世譽。

translations.literal: Bing's younger brother Xi, styled Guili, enjoyed inherited family repute.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's younger brother Xi, whose courtesy name was Guili, enjoyed inherited family repute.

sentences.zh: 歷司徒主簿、彭城王勰開府屬。

translations.literal: He served successively as chief clerk under the Minister of Works and a member of Prince of Pengcheng Xie's opening office staff.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as chief clerk under the minister of works and on the opening office staff of Prince of Pengcheng Xie.

sentences.zh: 遷幽州長史、博陵太守，吏民愛敬之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief secretary of Youzhou and Administrator of Bolling; officials and commoners loved and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief secretary of Youzhou and administrator of Bolling, where officials and commoners loved and respected him.

sentences.zh: 在郡九年，轉河東太守，卒於郡，年五十一。

translations.literal: After nine years in the commandery he was transferred to Administrator of Hedong; he died in the commandery at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years in office he was transferred to administrator of Hedong and died there at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈中山太守。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 孝昌三年，重贈後將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang he was posthumously granted again as General of the Rear and Regional Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaochang he was again posthumously made general of the rear and regional inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 長子世儒，字希業。

translations.literal: The eldest son Shiru, styled Xiye.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Shiru, whose courtesy name was Xiye.

sentences.zh: 卒於大司馬從事中郎。

translations.literal: He died while serving as attendant gentleman to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as attendant gentleman to the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 世儒第三弟叔業，武定中，南兗州別駕。

translations.literal: Shiru's third younger brother Shuye, during Wuding, served as Vice-Prefect of South Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiru's third younger brother Shuye, during Wuding, served as vice-prefect of South Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 秉從父弟廣，字仲慶，有議幹。

translations.literal: Bing's younger paternal cousin Guang, styled Zhongqing, had talent for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's younger paternal cousin Guang, whose courtesy name was Zhongqing, had talent for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 初為中書學生。

translations.literal: At first he was a student in the Masters of Writing school.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a student in the masters of writing school.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，殿中郎中，歷通直散騎侍郎、太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: During Emperor Gaozu's reign he was a bureau director in the palace and successively served as Unembellished Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Commandant of Footsoldiers for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Gaozu's reign he was a palace bureau director and successively served as unembellished attendant of the scattered cavalry and commandant of footsoldiers for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 詔守尚書左丞，父憂去職。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing; on his father's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him acting left assistant director of the masters of writing, but he left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 後任城王澄為揚州，引廣為鎮南府長史，以母老辭。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Rencheng Cheng was assigned to Yangzhou, he recruited Guang as chief secretary of the Pacify-the-South command, but Guang declined on grounds that his mother was elderly.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince of Rencheng Cheng went to Yangzhou, he recruited Guang as chief secretary of the pacify-the-south staff, but Guang declined because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 景明末，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the end of Jingming he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jingming era he died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈安遠將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted General Who Pacifies the Distance and Regional Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who pacifies the distance and regional inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子元獻，字世儁，頗有學識。

translations.literal: His son Yuanxian, styled Shijun, had considerable learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanxian, whose courtesy name was Shijun, had considerable learning.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，不行。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a Presented Scholar but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as a presented scholar but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 後卒於鄉里。

translations.literal: Later he died in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in his home district.

sentences.zh: 廣弟文業，為中書博士，轉司徒主簿。

translations.literal: Guang's younger brother Wenye served as erudite in the Masters of Writing and was transferred to chief clerk under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's younger brother Wenye served as an erudite in the masters of writing and was transferred to chief clerk under the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 城陽王鸞為定州刺史，引為治中。

translations.literal: When Prince of Chengyang Luan became Regional Inspector of Dingzhou, he recruited him as rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Chengyang Luan became regional inspector of Dingzhou, he recruited him as rectifier.

sentences.zh: 年四十九卒。

translations.literal: He died at age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子伯謙，武定末，司空諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His son Boqian, at the end of Wuding, was consulting member of the Minister of Works' staff.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boqian, at the end of Wuding, was a consulting member on the minister of works' staff.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李以儒俊之風，當旌帛之舉；

translations.literal: The historian writes: Li, with the air of a Confucian talent, was suited to the award of banners and silk;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Li, with the bearing of a Confucian talent, was fit for the award of banners and silk;

sentences.zh: 崔以文雅之烈，應利用之科。

translations.literal: Cui, with the distinction of literary refinement, answered to the category of those put to practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Cui, with the distinction of literary refinement, answered to the category of useful talent.

sentences.zh: 世家有業，餘慶不已，人位繼軌，亦為盛哉。

translations.literal: Lineages with established calling, blessings that do not cease—the succession of men and office is truly magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: Established lineages, blessings that never end, offices passed in succession—how splendid indeed.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 綜子遵 諸本「遵」作「道」。

translations.literal: "Zong's son Zun": in all editions "Zun" is written "Dao."
translations.idiomatic: "Zong's son Zun": in all editions Zun is written Dao.

sentences.zh: 北史卷三三李靈附李渾傳作「遵」。

translations.literal: Beishi juan 33, appended biography of Li Hun in Li Ling, reads "Zun."
translations.idiomatic: The appended biography of Li Hun in Li Ling, Beishi juan 33, reads Zun.

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「京兆王愉傳

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai says: "In the biography of Prince of Jingzhao Yu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai says: "In the biography of Prince of Jingzhao Yu

sentences.zh: 〈卷二二〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 22〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 22〉

sentences.zh: 『道』作『遵』，北齊書

translations.literal: "Dao" is written "Zun"; the Northern Qi Annals
translations.idiomatic: has Dao as Zun; the Northern Qi Annals

sentences.zh: 〈卷二九〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 29〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈juan 29〉

sentences.zh: 李渾傳同。

translations.literal: the biography of Li Hun agrees.
translations.idiomatic: the biography of Li Hun agrees.

sentences.zh: 疑此『道』字誤。」

translations.literal: I suspect this character "Dao" is in error."
translations.idiomatic: This suggests that Dao is in error."

sentences.zh: 按唐書卷七二上宰相世系表趙郡李氏東祖房下也作「遵」。

translations.literal: According to Tang Annals juan 72, upper, tables of ministerial lineage under the eastern branch of the Zhao Commandery Li clan, it also reads "Zun."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Annals (juan 72, upper), in the tables of ministerial lineage under the eastern branch of the Zhao Commandery Li clan, likewise reads Zun.

sentences.zh: 張說是，今據北史改。

translations.literal: Zhang's collation is correct; the text now follows Beishi in correction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's reading is accepted; the text is now corrected following Beishi.

sentences.zh: 繪弟系 北史卷三三「系」作「緯」。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Xi: in Beishi juan 33 "Xi" is written "Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Xi: Beishi juan 33 writes Xi as Wei.

sentences.zh: 按本名「緯」，魏收避北齊後主諱改作「系」。

translations.literal: His original name was "Wei"; Wei Shou changed it to "Xi" to avoid the taboo of the Northern Qi latter ruler.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Wei; Wei Shou changed it to Xi to avoid the taboo of the Northern Qi latter ruler.
