sentences.zh: 北齊書卷二九李渾傳作「偉」，是「緯」的形訛。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Annals juan 29, biography of Li Hun, reads "Wei," a graphic corruption of "Wei."
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi Annals (juan 29), biography of Li Hun, reads Wei in the sense of "great"—this is a graphic corruption of Wei in the sense of "latitude."

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍城陽公孔伯恭等率眾迎之 諸本「城陽」作「陽城」，北史卷三三作「城陽」。

translations.literal: "General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong and others led troops to welcome him": in all editions "Chengyang" is written "Yangcheng"; Beishi juan 33 reads "Chengyang."
translations.idiomatic: "General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong and others led troops to welcome him": in all editions Chengyang is written Yangcheng; Beishi juan 33 reads Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 按卷五一孔伯恭傳、卷六顯祖紀天安元年九月、卷五０尉元傳並作「城陽」，這裏「陽城」乃誤倒，今據乙。

translations.literal: According to juan 51 biography of Kong Bogong, juan 6 Annals of Xianzu ninth month of the first year of Tian'an, and juan 50 biography of Yu Yuan, all read "Chengyang"; here "Yangcheng" is a transposition error—it is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Kong Bogong (juan 51), the Annals of Emperor Xianzu (juan 6), ninth month of the first year of Tian'an, and the biography of Yu Yuan (juan 50) all read Chengyang; here Yangcheng is a transposition error and is now emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 陽平王頤之為定州 諸本「頤」作「顯」，北史卷三二崔鑒傳作「順」。

translations.literal: "Prince Yangping Yi as regional inspector of Dingzhou": in all editions "Yi" is written "Xian"; Beishi juan 32 biography of Cui Jian reads "Shun."
translations.idiomatic: "Prince Yangping Yi as regional inspector of Dingzhou": in all editions Yi is written Xian; the biography of Cui Jian in Beishi juan 32 reads Shun.

sentences.zh: 按元顯是陽平王熙孫，但其祖他已改封淮南王，墓誌集釋

translations.literal: According to this, Yuan Xian was grandson of Prince Yangping Xi, but his grandfather had already been re-enfeoffed as Prince of Huainan; Collected Explanations of Epitaphs
translations.idiomatic: Comment: Yuan Xian was grandson of Prince Yangping Xi, but his grandfather had already been re-enfeoffed as Prince of Huainan; the Collected Explanations of Epitaphs

sentences.zh: 〈圖版六七〉

translations.literal: 〈illustration plate six seven〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Plate 67〉

sentences.zh: 有元顯墓誌，父、祖都稱淮南王，顯所襲自然也是淮南王。

translations.literal: has Yuan Xian's epitaph; both father and grandfather are styled Prince of Huainan, so the title Xian inherited would naturally also be Prince of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: preserves Yuan Xian's epitaph; both father and grandfather are styled Prince of Huainan, so the title Xian inherited would naturally also be Prince of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 元順有三：一見卷一五昭成子孫傳，封毗陵王；

translations.literal: There are three Yuan Shun: one in juan 15 biography of the descendants of Zhaocheng, enfeoffed as Prince of Piling;
translations.idiomatic: There are three Yuan Shun: one in the biography of the descendants of Zhaocheng (juan 15), enfeoffed as Prince of Piling;

sentences.zh: 一見卷一九中任城王雲傳，封東阿公；

translations.literal: one in juan 19, middle, biography of Prince of Rencheng Yun, enfeoffed as Duke of Dong'e;
translations.idiomatic: one in the biography of Prince of Rencheng Yun (juan 19, middle), enfeoffed as Duke of Dong'e;

sentences.zh: 又一見北史卷一五宗室傳封濮陽王。

translations.literal: and another in Beishi juan 15 genealogy of the imperial clan, enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: and another in the genealogy of the imperial clan in Beishi juan 15, enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 別無陽平王順其人。

translations.literal: There is no other Prince Yangping Shun.
translations.idiomatic: There is no other Prince Yangping Shun.

sentences.zh: 據卷六八甄琛傳稱琛「後為本州陽平王頤衞軍府長史」。

translations.literal: According to juan 68 biography of Zhen Chen, which says Chen "later served as chief secretary of the guard army staff of Prince Yangping Yi."
translations.idiomatic: According to the biography of Zhen Chen (juan 68), Chen "later served as chief secretary of the guard army staff of Prince Yangping Yi."

sentences.zh: 琛為定州毋極人，本州即指定州，與此傳下文崔秉拳擊甄琛墜牀事相合。

translations.literal: Chen was a native of Wuji in Dingzhou; his home province was Dingzhou, which agrees with the account below in this biography of Cui Bing striking Zhen Chen and knocking him from the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was a native of Wuji in Dingzhou; his home province was Dingzhou, which agrees with the account below in this biography of Cui Bing striking Zhen Chen and knocking him from the bed.

sentences.zh: 知「顯」「順」都是「頤」的形訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Thus both "Xian" and "Shun" are graphic corruptions of "Yi"; the text is now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Thus both Xian and Shun are graphic corruptions of Yi; the text is now corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 太昌中除驃騎大將軍 諸本「驃」作「驍」，北史卷三二崔鑒附崔秉傳作「驃」。

translations.literal: During Taichang appointed General of Cavalry Who Spreads Martiality: in all editions "biao" is written "xiao"; the appended biography of Cui Bing in the biography of Cui Jian in Northern History chapter 32 reads "biao."
translations.idiomatic: During Taichang appointed General of Cavalry Who Spreads Martiality: in all editions biao is written xiao; the appended biography of Cui Bing in the biography of Cui Jian in Northern History chapter 32 reads biao.

sentences.zh: 按「驍騎」罕見加「大」之例。

translations.literal: According to this, the title "xiao cavalry" is rarely seen with the addition of "great."
translations.idiomatic: The title "xiao cavalry" is rarely seen with the addition of "great."

sentences.zh: 卷一一出帝紀太昌元年九月記「以車騎將軍左光祿大夫崔秉為驃騎大將軍」。

translations.literal: Juan 11 Annals of Emperor Chu, ninth month of the first year of Taichang, records "Cui Bing, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendor, was made General of Agile Cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Chu (juan 11), ninth month of the first year of Taichang, records that "Cui Bing, general of chariots and cavalry and left grand master of splendor, was made general of agile cavalry."

sentences.zh: 「驍」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: The character "xiao" is corrupt; it is now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao is a corruption; the text is now corrected accordingly.
